types.wordiness:
# Wordiness

Find an unnecessarily elaborate expression of a single point. Work out a shorter wording that preserves its meaning, qualifications, actor, timing and useful emphasis. Require an identifiable padded construction, rather than treating every sentence with a shorter paraphrase as defective.

Cover verbose cause, condition and purpose connectors, layered requests, generic nominalized actions, and nested identity, capability or role constructions. Judge their function across unfamiliar wording and settings. A genuine defect remains a hit beside informative details.

Preserve ordinary useful formal language, technical terms, meaningful capability or uncertainty, actual named operations or outputs, and decisions whose deliberation matters. Preserve unspecified actors when shortening. Long words, passive voice and nominalizations alone establish no defect.

Duplicated information belongs to redundancy. A disposable announcement around a supplied point belongs to unnecessary framing. This check needs additional unnecessary elaboration of the expression itself. Quotation marks protect wording being documented or examined; wording adopted by the writer still requires judgment.

## Hits

### Example 1

> Suppose twenty classes are assigned by lottery to use one of two textbooks. We compare their average test scores at the end of term. The difference between the two group averages **is what constitutes** our estimate of the textbook's effect.
>
> The lottery assigns whole classes rather than individual pupils, so pupils in the same class share both a teacher and a treatment. The uncertainty calculation must account for that grouping; treating every pupil as an independent observation would make the estimate appear more precise than it is.

### Example 2

> **Due to the fact that** the loading bay will be resurfaced, deliveries need to use the front entrance next week. Small parcels can come through reception. Pallets will need a timed slot so the driver can unload without blocking the pavement.
>
> I've put the temporary unloading schedule in the shared folder. Please add any expected pallets by Thursday lunchtime.

### Example 3

> The analysis **gives consideration to** household size by reporting spending per person as well as spending per household. Both measures are useful here: a larger household may spend more in total while spending less for each member. The appendix shows how shared purchases were allocated.

## No-Hits

### Example 1

> I've checked the meter readings on your account. The reading submitted on 6 September was entered against the upstairs meter, which explains the higher estimate on this bill.
>
> I can make an adjustment to the balance once you send a photo showing the downstairs meter's serial number and current reading. Please include both in the same photo if you can. Your payment date will stay the same while we sort this out.

### Example 2

> Northbank's scanner has the capability to read labels through the clear sleeves we use on returned boxes. The less expensive model needed the sleeve removed in four of our twenty trials. Both connected to the stock system without an adapter.
>
> For the returns bench, I'd choose Northbank. Removing sleeves slowed the test down, and we would need a bin beside the desk for the discarded plastic. The cheaper scanner would still suit the dispatch station, where the labels are exposed.

### Example 3

> The last bus had gone by the time we reached the stop. We stood under the shelter while Len checked the timetable on his phone. There was another route from the hospital, but it meant a walk uphill with the suitcase. After a few minutes we made the decision to call a taxi. It arrived before Len had finished putting the broken wheel back in his bag.

types.wordiness:
# Wordiness

Find an unnecessarily elaborate expression of a single point. Identify its padding and work out a shorter wording that preserves the claim, qualifications, actor, timing and useful emphasis. Merely replacing an ordinary expression with a shorter equivalent establishes no defect.

Cover verbose connectors, layered requests, generic nominalized actions, and nested identity, capability, role or location constructions. Identify removable scaffolding around the action or relation. A nominalized action plus a generic performance verb may become an actor-neutral passive verb; preserving an unspecified actor does not require preserving the nominalization.

Preserve ordinary useful formal language that directly expresses a relation, quantity, permission, capability, decision or operation. Assess what makes the construction unnecessarily elaborate, rather than treating an available shorter verb or connector as evidence. Preserve possibility versus actuality, duration versus timing, meaningful scope, deliberation, technical distinctions and established names. Long words, passive voice and nominalizations alone establish no defect.

Preserve wording being documented, translated or explained; assess the writer's surrounding assertions independently. Wording adopted by the writer remains assessable. Informative details leave independent padding intact. Duplicated information belongs to redundancy; a disposable announcement around a supplied point belongs to unnecessary framing.

## Hits

### Example 1

> **The replacement of expired keys will now be performed** automatically during the overnight maintenance window. Active connections keep their existing key until they reconnect. Administrators receive a summary of replacements at the address configured in Security Settings.

### Example 2

> **Due to the fact that** the loading bay will be resurfaced, deliveries need to use the front entrance next week. Small parcels can come through reception. Pallets will need a timed slot so the driver can unload without blocking the pavement.
>
> I've put the temporary unloading schedule in the shared folder. Please add any expected pallets by Thursday lunchtime.

### Example 3

> The hook should be **positioned in a location that is above** the centre of the basket. If it sits to one side, the basket will hang at an angle.
>
> Use a fixing suitable for the ceiling material and check its load rating with the basket full of damp compost. That weight can be considerably greater than the dry weight shown on the basket label.

## No-Hits

### Example 1

> The phrase 'for the purpose of making a claim' appears in the leaflet we are translating. Here 'claim' means requesting a payment from the insurer. Use the same term in the heading and the form instructions so readers can connect the two.

### Example 2

> The calendar now has the capacity to display two time zones side by side. Select the second zone in Calendar Preferences; your event times will still be stored in UTC.
>
> This view is available on tablets as well as desktop screens. On a phone, the second zone appears beneath each event.

### Example 3

> The migration changes how dates are stored, with the result that an export may show a different calendar date when opened in another time zone. The original timestamp remains available in the audit column. Check that column when reconciling overnight transactions.

types.wordiness:
# Wordiness

Read each suspected expression literally in the full passage before proposing an edit. Identify what its words contribute. Require both conditions for a hit:

- A specific shorter wording preserves the claim, actor, qualifications, timing and useful emphasis.
- The original contains identifiable padding or an unnecessarily elaborate construction. An available shorter synonym or equally good paraphrase satisfies only the first condition.

Distinguish direct ordinary formal wording from a detour through generic scaffolding around the point. Judge the detour, rather than the word count or grammatical category. A noun or auxiliary can name something the passage discusses or distinguishes; reducing it to the nearest verb may collapse that meaning. Preserve what the writer asserts, rather than merely its practical consequence.

Ordinary useful formal wording needs no special technical justification. Check its function before calling it padding. A nominalized action with only generic performance scaffolding can become an actor-neutral passive verb. This preserves an unspecified actor while removing the detour. Apply the same test across unfamiliar constructions, including elaborate identity and location expressions.

Preserve wording being documented, translated or explained; assess surrounding assertions independently. Judge wording adopted by the writer normally. Informative details leave independent padding intact. Duplicated information belongs to redundancy; a disposable announcement around a supplied point belongs to unnecessary framing.

## Paired Examples

### Relation Versus Scaffolding

#### Hit

> Suppose twenty classes are assigned by lottery to use one of two textbooks. We compare their average test scores at the end of term. The difference between the two group averages **is what constitutes** our estimate of the textbook's effect.
>
> The lottery assigns whole classes rather than individual pupils, so pupils in the same class share both a teacher and a treatment. The uncertainty calculation must account for that grouping; treating every pupil as an independent observation would make the estimate appear more precise than it is.

#### No-Hit

> Northbank's scanner has the capability to read labels through the clear sleeves we use on returned boxes. The less expensive model needed the sleeve removed in four of our twenty trials. Both connected to the stock system without an adapter.
>
> For the returns bench, I'd choose Northbank. Removing sleeves slowed the test down, and we would need a bin beside the desk for the discarded plastic. The cheaper scanner would still suit the dispatch station, where the labels are exposed.

The hit wraps an identity in extra scaffolding. The no-hit directly states a useful capability; a shorter modal paraphrase alone establishes no padding.

### Action Versus Referenced Output

#### Hit

> **The replacement of expired keys will now be performed** automatically during the overnight maintenance window. Active connections keep their existing key until they reconnect. Administrators receive a summary of replacements at the address configured in Security Settings.

#### No-Hit

> The fixed-price proposal includes removal of the old tank. The other supplier will make an assessment of access before quoting for removal, because its smaller crane may need a temporary position in the neighbour's yard. We should obtain that assessment before comparing the delivered prices.

The hit's performance frame can become a passive verb. The no-hit's assessment names an output to obtain and use; its noun construction serves that meaning.

### Cause Versus Fact Wrapper

#### Hit

> **Due to the fact that** the loading bay will be resurfaced, deliveries need to use the front entrance next week. Small parcels can come through reception. Pallets will need a timed slot so the driver can unload without blocking the pavement.
>
> I've put the temporary unloading schedule in the shared folder. Please add any expected pallets by Thursday lunchtime.

#### No-Hit

> The coach arrived late as a result of a lorry breaking down on the bypass. We waited in the school office, where the secretary found paper cups for the tea. By the time the driver called, the rain had stopped and everyone was outside checking which cases belonged to whom.

The hit adds a generic fact wrapper around its cause. The no-hit uses an ordinary causal expression; a shorter connector alone establishes no defect.

criteria.false: No identifiable unnecessary elaboration remains after checking literal meaning and ordinary formal usage. An equivalent shorter paraphrase alone establishes no defect.

wordiness.instructions: Does the writer's own wording contain unnecessary elaboration according to the wordiness definition and paired examples in state? Preserve expressions quoted for examination or documentation; judge the surrounding prose separately.

criteria.true: At least one construction takes an unnecessary verbal detour around its point. Removing that padding preserves the claim, actor, qualifications, timing and useful emphasis. A shorter ordinary paraphrase alone is insufficient.
